problem.problem:
Anne is blue. Anne is smart. Bob is green. Bob is round. Erin is rough. Harry is cold. Harry is kind. All kind things are round. If something is rough then it is round. All cold things are round. Round things are cold. All kind things are green. If something is smart then it is rough. If something is cold and not blue then it is rough. If Bob is smart then Bob is not green. All smart, cold things are kind.

Determine whether the following statement is true, false, or unknown:
Erin is smart.

Predicates:
Blue($x, bool) ::: Is x blue?
Smart($x, bool) ::: Is x smart?
Green($x, bool) ::: Is x green?
Round($x, bool) ::: Is x round?
Rough($x, bool) ::: Is x rough?
Cold($x, bool) ::: Is x cold?
Kind($x, bool) ::: Is x kind?

Facts:
Blue(Anne, True) ::: Anne is blue.
Smart(Anne, True) ::: Anne is smart.
Green(Bob, True) ::: Bob is green.
Round(Bob, True) ::: Bob is round.
Rough(Erin, True) ::: Erin is rough.
Cold(Harry, True) ::: Harry is cold.
Kind(Harry, True) ::: Harry is kind.

Rules:
Kind($x, True) >>> Round($x, True) ::: All kind things are round.
Rough($x, True) >>> Round($x, True) ::: If something is rough then it is round.
Cold($x, True) >>> Round($x, True) ::: All cold things are round.
Round($x, True) >>> Cold($x, True) ::: Round things are cold.
Kind($x, True) >>> Green($x, True) ::: All kind things are green.
Smart($x, True) >>> Rough($x, True) ::: If something is smart then it is rough.
Cold($x, True) && Blue($x, False) >>> Rough($x, True) ::: If something is cold and not blue then it is rough.
Smart(Bob, True) >>> Green(Bob, False) ::: If Bob is smart then Bob is not green.
Smart($x, True) && Cold($x, True) >>> Kind($x, True) ::: All smart, cold things are kind.

Query:
Smart(Erin, True) ::: Erin is smart.
